_comment: The authored prose the teardown page asserts, as data rather than as code.
Every VALUE on the page comes from assets/tokens.json, the manifest or the
provenance map. This file carries only the sentences, so what the page claims is
auditable in one place and editable without touching the renderer.
SKILL.md governs. If a sentence here disagrees with SKILL.md, SKILL.md is right and
promise: Strategy to execution, thinking and doing and everything in between.
promise_source: the cover subhead on the system's own cover, so it is the brand's words rather than a summary of them
traits_source: Taken verbatim from the house style, not inferred.

signature.title: The signature device · the emphasis clause
signature.rule: Every headline carries one emphasis clause, and it is always the last two to four words. The clause steps from #1F1F1F to pure #000000 on a light ground, or to white at 72% opacity on a dark one. It is a value step, never a colour change and never a weight change. On the type ladder it is the only place <em> appears.

arrow.title: The arrow is the second signature, and it is rarer
arrow.body: A single red arrow pointing into the first line of the cover headline. One per deck, on the cover only, and its horizontal placement is recomputed per word: at 176px Black, "AI" overhangs its box by 2px and "MAKE" sits 11px inside it. Never copy an arrow's position from another cover.

logo.lead: Two marks, and they never appear together. The full lockup takes the cover, dividers and the closing slide. The corner bug takes every interior slide.
geometry: 275 × 286 at x 1754, y 774. Bleeds 109px off the right edge and stops 20px above the bottom, not 56
73 × 38, inset 56, 239 inside the unit. Lands 37px from the right edge and 29px from the bottom
polygon(100% 0, 100% 50.39%, 50.37% 100%, 0 100%). Band thickness 101 perpendicular, mark centroid at 47% across it
logo.construction_note: This geometry was reconstructed by eye once and was wrong on all four axes for three revisions. It comes from the node now.
logo.variant_note: The bug ships in two variants and the choice is made by measuring the plate behind it, not by reading the ground class. A light ground carries .bug with the #F6F6F6 to #FFFFFF stripe; a gradient or photographic ground carries .bug--dark, whose stripe is white at 22% to 9% and whose mark inverts. One recipe has a light ground with a brand wedge in that corner, which is why the class is not the test.
files: The horizontal lockup. Cover, dividers, closing. White on dark, #1F1F1F on light
The mark inside the corner bug. Every interior slide
The same mark pre-inverted, for the export path where a CSS filter has no PowerPoint equivalent
The stripe's clip path, baked for export
The Brand X wedge pair on a cover. Bleeds off two edges on purpose
The cover arrow. One per deck
clearspace: The bottom-right 200 × 160 of every interior slide stays clear
210 × 44 on a 1920 canvas. Never scaled below it in a deck
Four things leave the canvas on purpose: the two Brand X wedges, the horizontal mesh at 32px right and 8px up, and the bug at 109px right
never: No stretch, skew, rotation, mirror or recolour
Never both marks on one slide. The lockup and the bug are alternatives, not a set
Never the bug reconstructed as polygons in an export. Five CSS features have no PowerPoint equivalent and ship pre-rendered
Never a lockup on an interior slide, and never a bug on the cover

color.lead: One blue, one purple that exists only as a gradient terminus, one red that is never a fill, and seven steps of ink. The system's colour is carried by gradients rather than by a palette.
color.purple_callout_title: The purple is not a colour you may use
color.purple_callout: #330072 appears only as the far stop of a gradient. There is no flat purple fill anywhere in the system, and the red is the same: it is the arrow and the stat direction mark, never a background and never type. One accent job, one red mark, one gradient surface per slide.
color.dark_note: The dark ground is the one to read twice. It is not the brand gradient darkened: #1D569E and #28115C are their own measured colours, lower in chroma and much lower in luminance, which is what lets it carry white type at 7.30:1 at its lightest point. Darkening the brand gradient instead gives you something that looks close and fails.
color.worst_title: The thinnest margin in the palette, and what it is not
color.worst_body: Against the gradient's light stop on its own this measures 3.75:1, which fails AA. No text ever sits on that stop alone, though: type spans a range of the surface, and the validator samples the rendered backdrop rather than a hex, so white body copy at the top of a tall --grad-brand-v panel measures 4.48:1 in situ and passes. The number to respect is the second one. Where the palette figure does bite is a SHORT element filled from the light end, a chip, a badge or a thin band, where the whole surface sits near the light stop and there is no range to fall into. At 20px or below, white on that surface needs 4.5:1 and does not have it. COL-04 catches it, measured, every time.
color.table_note: WCAG 2.0 relative luminance, computed at render time from the token values. These are PALETTE ratios, flat colour against flat colour. Every ratio the validator enforces is measured from the rendered backdrop instead, at the 90th percentile for light type and the 10th for dark, because a gradient and a photograph have no single hex. Read this table for the shape of the palette, never as the number a given slide will score. "AA large only" means the pairing clears 3:1 and is legal at 24px regular or 18.66px bold and above.

faces: Every headline, every display step, every stat. A separate family, not a weight.
Body, lede, caption, source. Bold at 700 for labels and the running header.
Bold italic, one job: the pull quote at 64px. Nothing else.
type.retired_title: Aptos ships its heavy cuts as separate families
type.retired_body: font-family:'Aptos'; font-weight:900 finds nothing, and the browser fakes a bold from Bold. Every headline renders light and every width you measure is fiction. That invalidated every measurement in this system until v1.7 and hid twenty-one real widows. Aptos Narrow was removed at v2.0 by direction: the token and both files are gone, so a reference to it is a bug, not a fallback.
type.scale_note: Set on a 1920 × 1080 canvas, so the steps above 76px are shown reduced to fit this page. The reduction is stated per row and the real size is the first number in the spec column. The two display steps are set white-space:nowrap on a real slide and wrap here only because this column is narrower than 1776.
rules: One headline per slide, three lines maximum, one emphasis clause on the last two to four words
Headlines are uppercase. Sentence case is one declared modifier, .t-h1--stmt, measured off node 1839:55, which changes exactly three things: leading to a flat 80px, tracking to -.05em, case off
Body copy holds one size step per job. Across a deck, no more than two steps of drift
Measure caps at 1176px left-aligned and 1776px centred, measured on the rendered line rects rather than the box
A hyphenated compound near the end of a measure is wrapped in .nb. Aptos has no U+2011, and a hyphen is its own break opportunity
A centred headline centres on 960 unless the source node genuinely sits off axis

samples.t-h1--stmt: AI is only valuable when people trust it.
samples.t-quote: We proved it on their data first.
samples.t-h3: Run AI your people rely on.
samples.t-lede: Strategy to execution, and everything in between.
samples.t-coversub: Thinking and doing and everything in between.
samples.t-body-l: Four hours a week, per analyst, measured over a quarter.
samples.t-body: We ran it against three quarters of their own ticket data.
samples.t-body-s: Same model, their data, no synthetic benchmark.
samples.t-caption: Measured on the rendered page, not inferred from the CSS.

shape.lead: Square by default. Two shadows, and a gradient surface gets neither.
radii: the default: panels, bands, chips and badges are square
the inner screen of that device
the process medallion and the ring
shape.radius_note: Every non-zero radius belongs to one named component. There is no general radius token, because a panel is square.
rules: A white panel carries --shadow-panel and its own 40/48 inset. Text closer than 24px to a panel edge is a warning, closer than 12px a failure
A gradient panel carries no shadow. A coloured surface does not need lifting off a grey one
No grey card on a white ground. Elevation runs light-on-light, and inverting it reads as a disabled state
No panel more than 35% empty below its last line of content. An empty panel is ground, not content
shape.gap: The template this page is derived from asks for an interaction signature and a working hover demo. A slide has no hover. The buttons in this system are drawn objects, not controls, and the deck ships as HTML or PPTX with no interaction layer at all. The motion section is deleted for the same reason.

space.lead: A twelve-column grid on a fixed 1920 × 1080 canvas. Spans sum to twelve, and nothing but photography and the Brand X crosses the margin.
rhythm: 40px vertical, 48px horizontal. The modal inset across the recipes
24px, 20px of space below it, then the headline
space.note: The nine-step scale is the spacing vocabulary. Anything between two steps is a number somebody typed.

dark.title: The dark emphasis surface
dark.lead: A second ground, and a rationed one. Node 1892:32, capped at one slide in five and never two in a row.
dark.note: The ground ships as a pair: the gradient and its own mesh, .mesh--dark at 2384px wide and offset -262px left, are one device. The emphasis clause inverts on this surface, stepping to white at 72% rather than to black, and the bug switches to its dark variant. It is an emphasis ground rather than a theme: there is no dark mode of the whole system, and a deck that runs dark throughout has no emphasis left to spend.

imagery.do_title: The library, and how much of it to use
do: Real people at real work: an engineer at an equipment wall, two people at one laptop, the ATC lobby. Each photograph carries its own crop list.
Holographic red-and-blue light is the house AI treatment and it is the one abstract family allowed, because it is the brand's own commissioned art rather than stock.
One in five slides carries a photograph at a real crop, and never more than six slides in a row without one. IMG-05 and IMG-06 fail a deck that drops below it.
Type over a photograph carries a measured scrim. The ratio is sampled from the rendered backdrop at the 90th percentile, never inferred from the CSS.
never: No crop outside the ones in the manifest. A new crop is a new ratio nobody measured.
No photograph used above its native resolution. Three in the library carry a warning and cannot fill the crops they are listed for.
No type baked into an image. Everything is live and selectable, or the PPTX is a screenshot deck.
No mesh inside a panel, a card, a media box or a band. Background only, and a direct child of the slide.
imagery.mesh_note: The real vector, all 882 diamond paths, windowed onto the middle of the artwork. The first attempt at this specimen took the first 150 paths and rendered an empty box, which is the whole point of the variant rule: the fade to transparent at both ends is baked into the artwork in absolute page coordinates, so the paths at the top-left of the file are genuinely invisible. That is why the same node exported from three positions returns three byte-identical files, and why the variant has to match the placement rather than the filename. Half-drop tessellation, one lattice period 53.528px.
mesh_variants: The extended asset, one lattice period wider. Centred content
Right-anchored with a 32px bleed and 8px up
left:-262. Pairs with the dark ground and only with it
imagery.mesh_footer: Opacity .11, and the blend is plus-lighter against the page surface. Half the recipes carry a mesh; every light-ground content slide carries some background device, and a deck that carries none is not using the system, it is using the grid.

voice.lead: Warm and direct. Blue-collar rather than boardroom. Aspirational only where it has been earned, and never performed.
voice.use_list: ticket, analyst, quarter, shop floor, procurement
voice.avoid_list: leverage, transform, seamless, robust, synergy, cutting-edge, game-changing, AI-powered as a bare adjective
voice.emdash: No em dashes anywhere. A comma, or two sentences. It applies to slide copy exactly as it applies to a memo, and it is the rule most often broken by whoever is drafting fast.
headlines: Everyone is buying AI. Fewer than 1 in 4 is getting paid back.
See it work on your data before you commit.
AI is only valuable when people trust it.
voice.headline_note: Two beats, the second one shorter, and the emphasis clause carries the payoff. Every claim gets a number or a name: "saves time" is banned, "four hours a week per analyst" is the standard.
voice.proof_note: Counted from the system at render time. These are facts about the system rather than client-facing proof numbers: the brand's verified claims live in each deck's source material and none are hard-coded here.

hard_rules: Every number in the system was measured off a Figma node. A value typed from memory is a value that has drifted.
Nothing is correct because it looks correct
A headline at 1.16:1, a logo wrong on four axes, twenty-one widows and a whole deck in a substituted typeface all passed visual review first.
An empty page is a defect in the same way an overfull one is, and it is the more common one. Ninety-one slides once passed with 8% median coverage.
One accent job, one red mark, one gradient surface, one background device. Two devices on a page is two arguments.
Nested in a panel its plus-lighter blend composites against the panel fill instead of the page, and the PPTX path drops it entirely.
The dark ground is capped at one slide in five
It is an emphasis ground. A deck where every page shouts has no emphasis left, and two dark slides in a row are emphatic against nothing.
Nothing but photography and the Brand X crosses them. Spans sum to twelve, no orphan columns.
Sampled from the rendered backdrop on every type-over-image and type-over-gradient pairing. WCAG 2.0 AA is the floor.
No em dashes in any WWT prose
House style. A comma or two sentences. It applies to slide copy as much as to a memo.
gaps: This system has no positioning work behind it. Nobody has written down where WWTDigital sits between any two poles, so the identity section states the promise and the traits and stops. Inventing axes would put a guess into everything downstream.
A 1920 × 1080 static page has no durations and no easings. If the system ever ships an animated export, this is the section that has to be written first.

The one unchecked exemption in the rule set. It excuses an element from the margin and centring rules on the claim that the Figma node genuinely sits off the grid, which is a fact about the source the validator cannot see. Twelve of the twenty recipes use it legitimately, so a ceiling on it would fail correct work.
